solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Blair cracked boring, licentious jokes (8)

indicatorNotes.cracked: something cracked is broken apart, so BLAIR's letters are smashed and reassembled

blocks.note: BLAIR rearranged
a dry speech is a boring one

annotation.surface: A dull former prime minister tries his hand at telling smutty jokes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cracked jokes' is the natural reading, but 'cracked' belongs to Blair, and 'jokes' ends the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Ribaldry is coarse, bawdy humour — licentious jokes in a single word.

entries.clue: Kid not allowed spicy food (6)

blocks.note: to kid or rag someone is to tease them
out = not allowed, as in 'smoking is out'

annotation.surface: A child is forbidden anything hot and spicy to eat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Kid' is a verb here, not a child: to rag someone is to tease them.
annotation.definitionFit: A ragout is a highly seasoned stew of meat and vegetables.

entries.clue: One missed among orders taken by good French dramatist (3,6)

indicatorNotes.missed: one (I) is missed, so it drops out of the word
indicatorNotes.taken by: the orders are taken in by BON, which holds them

blocks.note: bon is French for good; it goes round the next piece
ENJOINS (orders) with I (one) missing

annotation.surface: A French playwright is short-listed as good, though one of his orders went astray.
annotation.walkthrough: The French in the surface belongs to 'good', not the dramatist: Ben Jonson was English, Shakespeare's contemporary.
annotation.definitionFit: Ben Jonson was a Jacobean playwright, author of Volpone and The Alchemist.

entries.clue: Prison sentence involving bird for criminal? (7)

indicatorNotes.involving: to involve is to take in, so LIFE takes OWL inside it

blocks.note: a life sentence; it wraps round OWL
an owl is a bird

annotation.surface: A long jail term awaits someone who did something to a bird.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bird' is also slang for prison time, which pulls it towards the sentence; here it is just an owl.
annotation.definitionFit: A lowlife is a disreputable person, often a petty criminal.

entries.clue: Hurried round to shop (3,2)

indicatorNotes.round: RAN goes round TO, holding it inside

blocks.note: ran = hurried; it goes round TO
used as it stands

annotation.surface: Someone dashed out to the shops.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shop' is the British slang verb for informing on someone to the police, not a store.
annotation.definitionFit: To shop someone is to betray them to the authorities, exactly to rat on them.

entries.clue: Always a cool head in charge, step back (3,3)

indicatorNotes.back: PACE is taken back, so it reads right to left

blocks.note: i/c is the abbreviation for in charge
PACE (step) reversed

annotation.surface: Advice to a leader: stay calm and step back from the fray.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition reads like praise for an unflappable boss; it describes a mountain top that is permanently frozen.
annotation.definitionFit: An ice cap is permanent ice covering a summit or pole — a head that is always cool.

entries.clue: One shrieking denied son milk substitute (7)

indicatorNotes.denied: the word is denied its S, which is taken away

blocks.note: SCREAMER without S (son)

annotation.surface: A howling baby is refused its milk and given formula instead.
annotation.walkthrough: S for son is the standard abbreviation from genealogies.
annotation.definitionFit: Creamer is a non-dairy powder or liquid used in place of milk in coffee.

entries.clue: Carpenter put power in lives, overseen by church (5)

indicatorNotes.put: to put something somewhere is to place it, so power is placed within the lives
indicatorNotes.in: in means inside, so the power sits within the letters for lives
indicatorNotes.overseen by: in a down clue, CH sits above the rest

blocks.note: CH is the abbreviation for church; it goes on top
he lives = he is; it holds P
P is the symbol for power

annotation.surface: A carpenter wired electricity into people's homes under the church's supervision.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Chips' is the traditional nickname for a ship's carpenter, from the wood chips he makes.
annotation.definitionFit: Chips was the name given to a ship's carpenter in the Royal Navy.

entries.clue: Operate bike going round established base (8)

indicatorNotes.going round: PEDAL goes round EST, enclosing it

blocks.note: you pedal a bike; it goes round EST
est. is the abbreviation for established

annotation.surface: Someone cycles in circles around an old military base.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Base' looks like the army camp being circled; it is the support a statue stands on.
annotation.definitionFit: A pedestal is the base supporting a column or statue.

entries.clue: Constriction sets in so badly (8)

indicatorNotes.badly: the letters are set in a bad order and need rearranging

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

annotation.surface: A tightening sets in so severely that it becomes a problem.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a symptom report, which suits a medical answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Stenosis is the medical term for an abnormal narrowing of a passage in the body.

entries.clue: High tide: newt now swimming in famous picture (4,4,3,4)

indicatorNotes.swimming: letters that are swimming move about freely and settle in a new order

blocks.note: the fifteen letters to rearrange

annotation.surface: With the tide in, a newt takes a swim, captured in a well-known painting.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Picture' sounds like a painting; here it is a motion picture, the 1939 film.
annotation.definitionFit: Gone with the Wind is the celebrated 1939 film, a famous picture in the cinema sense.

entries.clue: Ideal university best in surrounding area (7)

indicatorNotes.in surrounding: IN surrounds A, holding it in the middle

blocks.note: U is the abbreviation for university
top = best
used as it stands; it wraps round A
A is the abbreviation for area

annotation.surface: The perfect university is the best one in the district.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word; it is a piece of the answer that goes round A.
annotation.definitionFit: Utopian describes an ideal, perfect society.

entries.clue: Goddess, saint and Magi from the East, not West (7)

indicatorNotes.from the East: in an across clue, reading from the east means right to left
indicatorNotes.not West: 'not' negates West, so its abbreviation W must be absent from the result

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for saint
the Magi are the three Wise Men
remove W from NEMESIWS

annotation.surface: A goddess joins a saint and the three kings travelling from the East.
annotation.walkthrough: The Magi really did come from the East, so the reversal hides in plain sight. S + WISEMEN reads NEMESIWS backwards; dropping W leaves the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A proper name used as the definition: the Greek goddess of retribution, whose name now also means any agent of downfall.

entries.clue: Religious rite snake vocally encourages? (8)

indicatorNotes.vocally: said with the voice, so the word is heard, not spelt

blocks.note: an asp is a snake
urges = encourages, spelt to fit the answer

annotation.surface: A church ritual that a snake seems to be egging on.
annotation.walkthrough: The homophone only has to work for the ending: ASP is spelt normally, and 'urges' supplies the sound -ERGES.
annotation.definitionFit: The Asperges is the rite of sprinkling the congregation with holy water before Mass.

entries.clue: Worker at Versailles possibly planting forest in Germany (8)

indicatorNotes.planting: to plant is to set something in the ground, so the forest is set inside another word
indicatorNotes.in: in means inside, naming Germany as the word that receives the forest

blocks.note: GER is the abbreviation for Germany; it holds ARDEN
the Forest of Arden, in Warwickshire and in As You Like It

annotation.surface: A labourer at the French palace might be planting trees in Germany.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Planting' is both the container instruction and a gardener's job. Versailles is famous for its formal gardens.
annotation.definitionFit: The palace of Versailles has vast gardens, so a worker there may well be a gardener.

entries.clue: Inferior cricketer leaves B&B with a side (5)

indicatorNotes.leaves: the two Bs leave the word, which is left without them

blocks.note: RABBIT, a poor batsman, without B and B
used as it stands

annotation.surface: A second-rate cricketer checks out of his guesthouse to join a team.
annotation.walkthrough: A rabbit is cricket slang for a hopeless batsman. 'Side' looks like a cricket team; it is a side dish.
annotation.definitionFit: Raita is a yoghurt side dish served with Indian food.

entries.clue: Barge in Bury rent free (9)

indicatorNotes.rent: rent means torn apart, so FREE is ripped up and reassembled

blocks.note: to inter is to bury
FREE rearranged

annotation.surface: A narrowboat moored in the Lancashire town of Bury without paying any rent.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Barge' and 'Bury' read as a boat and the Lancashire town; the capital B is the setter's disguise for the verb bury. 'Rent' is torn, not payment.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: barging in on other people's business means meddling uninvited.

entries.clue: Bull almost hit cow? (8)

indicatorNotes.almost: almost the whole word: its last letter is dropped

blocks.note: BELT (hit) without its last letter
a cow lows, so it is a lower

annotation.surface: A bull very nearly strikes a cow.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cow' looks like the animal and nothing else, but the setter reads it as 'one that lows'; the question mark flags that and the bull as one that bellows.
annotation.definitionFit: A bull bellows, so it is a bellower; the question mark marks the definition by example.

entries.clue: Year one sits periodically for artist (5)

indicatorNotes.periodically: at regular intervals: every other letter is taken

blocks.note: the even letters of yEaR oNe SiTs

annotation.surface: Each year a pupil sits for a portrait by a painter.
annotation.walkthrough: Max Ernst was a German-born surrealist painter.
annotation.definitionFit: Max Ernst was a leading Dada and Surrealist artist.

entries.clue: Faster animal embracing hard time (7)

indicatorNotes.embracing: TIGER embraces H and T, holding them inside

blocks.note: a tiger is an animal; it holds H and T
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
T is the abbreviation for time

annotation.surface: A quicker beast hugs its way through a tough stretch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Faster' suggests speed, but it means more firmly fixed, as in 'hold fast'.
annotation.definitionFit: Fast can mean firmly fixed, so faster is tighter.

entries.clue: Thunder from returning beak judge welcomes (8)

indicatorNotes.returning: NOSE comes back, so it reads right to left

blocks.note: to rate is to judge; it holds ESON
NOSE (beak) reversed

annotation.surface: A thunderous rebuke from a magistrate back on the bench, which a judge welcomes.
annotation.walkthrough: In British slang a beak is a magistrate, which is where the surface wants it; here it is just a nose.
annotation.definitionFit: To thunder is to boom and reverberate, which is to resonate.

entries.clue: Previously unrivalled thing in Rome not so great? (7)

indicatorNotes.in Rome: the next word is put into Latin, the language of Rome

blocks.note: non is Latin for not
such = so great, as in 'such a fuss'

annotation.surface: Rome's former glory is not so great as it once was.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Previously' flags an archaic word: nonsuch is an old term for something without equal.
annotation.definitionFit: A nonsuch (or nonesuch) was a person or thing without equal, now archaic.

entries.clue: Problem steamship coming into sound (6)

indicatorNotes.coming into: SS comes into HALE, going inside it

blocks.note: sound = healthy = hale; it takes SS inside
SS is the prefix for steamship

annotation.surface: A steamship runs into trouble entering a stretch of water.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sound' reads as a body of water, which suits a ship; here it means healthy.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in informal speech: a nuisance or bother of any kind.

entries.clue: Way to get to grips with spinach dish (7)

indicatorNotes.to get to grips with: LANE grips SAG, holding it inside

blocks.note: a lane is a way; it holds SAG
sag (saag) is spinach in Indian cooking

annotation.surface: How to deal with a plate of spinach.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spinach dish' reads as one phrase, but spinach is wordplay; the definition is only 'dish'. Sag is the Hindi word for spinach, familiar from curry-house menus.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by genus: the answer is one particular baked Italian pasta dish, so 'dish' is its broad class.

entries.clue: Upright female in small fedora? (5)

indicatorNotes.in: in means inside, so the female sits within the letters for the fedora

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a fedora is a hat; it holds F
F is the abbreviation for female

annotation.surface: A respectable woman wearing a little trilby-style hat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Upright' reads as a moral adjective describing the woman; it is a noun, a vertical post. The question mark marks fedora as an example of a hat.
annotation.definitionFit: Noun sense of upright: a vertical post, pole or column, as in the shaft of a pillar.

entries.clue: Maidens popular with killer in holiday island (7)

blocks.note: M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for maiden overs
in = popular, fashionable
the orca is the killer whale

annotation.surface: Young women going out with a murderer on a Mediterranean break.
annotation.walkthrough: A maiden is a cricket over with no runs scored, recorded as M.
annotation.definitionFit: Minorca (Menorca) is a Balearic island popular with holidaymakers.

entries.clue: Yacht sanctuary keeps out November seas (5)

indicatorNotes.keeps out: N is kept out of the word

blocks.note: MARINA without N (November in the NATO alphabet)

annotation.surface: A harbour shelters boats from the stormy November seas.
annotation.walkthrough: The seas here are on the Moon: its dark plains were named maria, Latin for seas.
annotation.definitionFit: Maria is the plural of mare, a lunar sea.

entries.clue: Pathetic people causing stir outside Globe are in control (4,3,8)

indicatorNotes.outside: WET ROUSERS goes outside EARTH, wrapping it

blocks.note: wet = feeble; with ROUSERS it wraps round EARTH after its W
the globe is the Earth
rousers are people who stir things up

annotation.surface: Hopeless troublemakers are running the Globe theatre.
annotation.walkthrough: The Globe in the surface sounds like Shakespeare's theatre; it is just the Earth. WETROUSERS splits after its first letter to take EARTH.
annotation.definitionFit: To wear the trousers is to be the one in charge, especially in a household.

entries.clue: Stand on lab bench or counter (6)

blocks.note: a noun: a piece of glassware standing on a chemistry bench
a verb: to answer back sharply

annotation.surface: Something is left standing on a laboratory bench or a shop counter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stand' looks like the verb; it is a noun for the thing standing. 'Counter' is the verb, not a worktop.
annotation.definitionFit: A retort is a long-necked distilling flask; to retort is to counter sharply.

entries.clue: Fine fabric green: nothing better (8)

blocks.note: green is slang for money, from US banknotes
mere = nothing more than, as in 'a mere child'

annotation.surface: A fine green fabric that nothing can beat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Green' reads as the fabric's colour; it is money.
annotation.definitionFit: Cashmere is a fine, soft wool fabric from the Kashmir goat.
